mcat_description.short: Light Gauge Framing System (LGSF) is a prefabricated structural building system using cold-formed galvanized steel sections (studs, tracks, joists, trusses) to create load-bearing frames for walls, floors, and roofs, sold as a complete engineered system or as fabricated profiles for on-site assembly.
mcat_description.long: LGSF is a construction technology in which thin galvanized steel sheets (typically 0.8–3mm thickness, 120–275 GSM coating) are cold-formed into structural sections — C-studs, U-tracks, floor joists, and roof trusses — that are prefabricated off-site and assembled on-site without welding, using screws and bolts. The system is designed to Indian Standards (BIS) for load, seismic, and wind resistance, and is validated by BMTPC Performance Appraisal Certificates (PAC) in India. LGSF is primarily suited for low-to-mid-rise buildings (G+1 to G+4 and above with hybrid systems), offering construction speeds up to 3x faster than conventional RCC/brick masonry with significantly lower dead weight. In India, the technology is gaining rapid adoption in residential housing (including PMAY government schemes), commercial buildings, schools, hospitals, and labour accommodation, with key manufacturers operating FrameCAD roll-forming lines in Chandigarh, Pune, Bangalore, and NCR.

market_context: Light Gauge Steel Framing (LGSF) is an emerging-to-mainstream construction technology in India, based on cold-formed galvanized steel sections manufactured off-site and assembled on-site without welding. The technology is validated in India through BMTPC Performance Appraisal Certificates (PAC) and must comply with BIS standards for load, seismic (IS:1893), and wind resistance parameters. The residential end-use segment dominates the Indian market (approximately 44% share), driven significantly by government affordable housing schemes including Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY); commercial end-use is the fastest-growing segment. The market is bifurcated by frame type: wall-bearing frames (dominant, suited for low-rise residential), skeleton frames (growing, suited for multi-storey commercial and industrial), and long-span frames (industrial applications). Key Indian manufacturers include EPACK Prefab, Stratus Steel, GalvaStrong (Mitsumi Housing), Indue Prefab, Pressmach, and Tata Steel's Nest-In (HabiNest brand), operating FrameCAD roll-forming lines. Standard section sizes in the Indian market are 89mm and 150mm profiles; galvanizing specification is typically 120–275 GSM with 0.8–3mm base metal thickness. The system is positioned as an RCC/brick masonry alternative offering construction speeds up to 3x faster, 70–80% lighter dead weight, and suitability for seismic and high-wind zones. The abbreviation LGSF is the dominant buyer-facing term in India; LGFS (transposed) also appears in search data. British Standard BS 5950-05 and Indian Standards are both referenced in BMTPC technical documentation for design compliance.
